reading: Each row is three runs: left colour, middle colour, right colour. In every row the middle run slides left until its right end is at the leftmost right end of any middle run (stopping at column 0 if it gets there first). The left colour fills the cells it leaves behind.
verb: slide row runs left to a common right edge

slots.subject: the middle-colour run in each row
slots.line: M = min over rows of the middle run's right end
slots.shift: min(run start, run end - M), to the left
slots.filler: left colour fills the vacated cells

why: after the shift every middle run ends at column M, or starts at column 0; run lengths are kept
invariants: middle run length in each row

reading: Two rectangles are joined by a one-cell-wide arm that has the colour of one of them. That rectangle slides along the arm until it touches the other rectangle, and the arm is erased.

slots.subject: the rectangle body that has the line arm
slots.path: the arm (a straight one-cell line from the body to the other rectangle)
slots.after: the body moves by the arm's length and ends in contact; the arm cells become background

why: the moved body keeps its rectangle shape, touches the fixed rectangle, and no arm cells remain

reading: Three 4x4 panels of 5s, separated by 0 columns, each have a hole pattern. Each panel becomes one row of a 3x3 output, coloured by its pattern: no hole -> 2, 2x2 centre hole -> 8, hole in the bottom-middle two rows -> 4, holes on the left and right edges of the middle rows -> 3.

slots.parts: panels cut by the all-0 separator columns (left to right)
slots.key: hole pattern -> colour: full=2, centre=8, bottom=4, sides=3 (learned from train)
slots.output: 3x3; row i is the colour of panel i

why: every training panel's hole pattern maps to its output row colour by one fixed table
invariants: panel order is the row order

reading: From each single coloured cell a line in its own colour runs right to the border. It then turns down the rightmost column and stops just above the next cell's line, or at the bottom border.
why: every marker's line reaches the right border, then runs down the last column until the row before the next marker's row (or the grid bottom), never crossing another line

reading: A loose shape of 8s is placed into the interior of a frame whose four sides have four different colours. Each 8 cell takes the colour of the nearest side, and stays 8 on a tie. The output is the frame's box.
verb: insert shape into frame and colour by nearest side

slots.unit: the 8-coloured shape (its box is the same size as the frame interior)
slots.container: the frame made of four one-colour sides with blank corners
slots.recolour: each shape cell -> colour of the side at least distance; equidistant -> stays 8

why: the output is the frame box with the 8-shape copied into its interior and recoloured by nearest side
invariants: the shape's cell positions inside the interior

reading: Count each colour's cells. The output has one column per colour, ordered by count from most to least. Each column is filled from the top with that colour, as many cells as its count, and the rest is 0. Output height is the largest count.

slots.columns: colours sorted by pixel count, largest first
slots.bar: column filled from the top, height = count
slots.size: rows = max count, cols = number of colours

why: each output column has exactly as many cells of its colour as the input

reading: The grid is split into an 8-coloured part and a 1-coloured part. The 2-objects slide horizontally to the edge of their part: left in the 8 part, right in the 1 part.
verb: slide objects to a side of their half

slots.panels: the two solid-colour halves (no separator line; the split is where the colour changes)
slots.direction: the panel's colour sets it: 8 -> left, 1 -> right

why: within each half every 2-object keeps its shape and its rows, and touches the half's left (8) or right (1) edge

reading: There are two big regions, each holding an inner rectangle. Each defect on an inner rectangle's edge (a dent into it, or a single cell sticking out of it) becomes a 2-cell bar across that edge, in the other big region's colour. For a dent the bar is the dent cell plus the cell just outside it; for a bump it is the bump cell plus the cell just inside it.
verb: mark rectangle defects with partner-colour dominoes

slots.containers: the two large regions (each a big rectangle of one colour)
slots.subject: the inner rectangle in each region
slots.defects: dents (container colour on the rectangle's edge) and bumps (single inner-colour cells just outside the edge)
slots.mark: a 2-cell bar perpendicular to the edge, covering the defect and its neighbour across the edge

why: only the cells of these bars change, and each bar takes the partner region's colour
invariants: all cells not in a defect bar

reading: In each row, every run of 3s slides left until it touches an 8 or the left border.
verb: slide left per row until blocked

slots.subject: horizontal runs of colour 3, each row on its own

why: every 3-run keeps its length and ends next to the first 8 to its left, or at column 0

reading: The 2 cells are grouped into 3x3 windows. Each window has a 5 at its centre and no 0 in it, and together the windows cover every 2. In each window the centre becomes 4 and the other 5s become 7. The 2s stay.

slots.windows: 3x3 boxes with no 0, a 5 at the centre, and no 2 in the ring around them, chosen so every 2 lies in exactly one box (4 boxes per grid in train)

why: every changed cell lies in a window; every 2 is in a window
